html:
SMTO-EVT-0003 — SMTO can't find that schedule or run

GUID: 67a4bf7e-b1d9-4d78-af4d-16daa718d899
Slug: event-not-found
Domain: EVT · Subsystem: evt

What happened

  • The schedule or run you chose no longer exists here. It may have been deleted, or the page was showing an out-of-date list. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the Schedules page. The page may have shown a schedule that was deleted or changed in another window.
  2. Use the search box, or select Clear search and filter, to look for the schedule. If it isn't there, it was deleted. A filter can hide a schedule, so clear it before deciding it's gone.
  3. If you were opening an earlier run, open the schedule and choose the run from its Recent runs list. Only runs that belong to that schedule can be opened from it.
  4. If the schedule was deleted and you still need it, select New schedule and create it again. A deleted schedule can't be run or edited, so a new one is needed.

What success looks like

  • The schedule appears in the list and your action works on it.

If it still fails

  • If the schedule is listed but still shows this error, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Scheduled event lookup failed (404): no non-deleted scheduled event has this ID, or the requested event run is absent or belongs to a different event.

What this means

  • Event lookup finds no current scheduled event, finds a deleted/non-scheduled record, or an event-run lookup is absent or belongs to another event. Event, monitor and notification identities have separate owners. Rejected control or missing notification does not cancel an existing task; only authoritative run state establishes its outcome.

Why this can happen

  • Event lookup finds no current scheduled event, finds a deleted/non-scheduled record, or an event-run lookup is absent or belongs to another event.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact current event and run ownership instead of reusing a removed identity.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the event_id with GET /api/agent/events (include_deleted=true shows soft-deleted records) and that event_run_id belongs to that event. Refresh client state and target an existing scheduled event; do not substitute a different event or reuse a deleted run ID.
  • Refresh scheduled events and open an existing event or retained event run. Do not reuse a deleted run identity.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The action targets a current observed event and its own retained run.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Event, monitor and notification identities have separate owners. Rejected control or missing notification does not cancel an existing task; only authoritative run state establishes its outcome.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
